Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 728/18 Fir no.: 242/19 Ps : Slc U/s : 279/338 Ipc Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Cnr No.:DLSE01-005355-2018 Umesh Paswan S/o Sh. Pradeep Paswan R/o Vaishali Dhanvari, Vaishali, Bihar. ......Claimant/Petit Versus 1. Shivam S/o Vinod Panchal R/o H. No. C-5, Gali no.3, Indra Niketan, Shahdra, Delhi. ............Driver cum owner/Respondent no. 1 3. The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. C-93, Subhash Road, Naveen Shahdra, Delhi. .........Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Date of accident : 19.09.2019 Date of filing of Dar : 30.10.2021 Date of Decision : 12.09.2022 Mact No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Page No. 1 of 25 Award 1.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 19.09.2019, at about 07.00 PM, petitioner went to a shop near Indraprashta Park to purchase a match box and when he was returning back from the shop and tried to cross the road, a police official stopped him saying that "VVIP Route laga hai thodi der bad road paar kar lena" . Then he waited for crossing the road and after clearance of VVIP route when he was crossing the road, all of a sudden, offending vehicle bearing no. DL 5SCE 7225 which was driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and in zig zag way hit him and due to forceful impact, he fell Umesh Paswan vs . Shivam & Ors. on 12 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98978415/ 1 down on the road and received grievous injuries. Injured/ petitioner was removed to JPN Apex Trauma Center, AIIMS Hospital, New Delhi where his MLC no.500196195/2019 was prepared. He discharged from the said hospital on 22.09.2019 and thereafter, he attended OPD treatment as outdoor patient in the said hospital. Thereafter, he went to his native place and admitted in Shashi Ortha & Trauma Hospital, Muzaffarpur, Bihar on 09.10.2019 to 20.10.2019 and treatment was given and surgery was also done in the said hospital. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 12.04.2022 noticing 27% permanent physical impairment in relation to left lower limb. Page No. 2 of 25 3. An FIR in question bearing No. 242/19, u/s 279,338 IPC PS Sunlight Colony, New Delhi was registered in this case. 4. As per record, R-1/ driver cum owner appeared in the present case but no reply filed by him. 5. But reply filed by R-2/insurance company. In nutshell, in reply filed by insurance company in question, it is stated that injured himself was negligent for the accident and because of his fault, accident in question took place, it is further claimed that R-1/ driver motorcycle was hit by unknown vehicle from behind. It it further stated that overwriting in the MLC of the injured. As such, it is stated that no claim is payable by insurance company. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 07.12.2021 by my Ld. Predecessor: 1. OPP. 2. 7. Petitioner filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. He relied upon various documents Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/E. PW-1 It may be noted that driver cum owner/ R-1 did not lead any evidence nor he cross examined the petitioner. But it is pertinent to note that insurance company/ R-2 examined driver cum owner/ R-1 as R3W1 as a summoned witness. Further, R-1 also appeared at the time of final argument and he also made his submissions. Further, Ld. counsel for petitioner as well as respondent insurance company filed written arguments. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude MACT No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. In present case, injured/ eye witness to the accident, PW-1 has deposed about the manner of accident and further deposed that accident occurred due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle. Petitioner proved on record his medical bills as Ex.PW1/4 (colly).
texts.arguments: 12. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s the relevant section is sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: MACT No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Page No. 7 of 25 (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Accordingly, it is taken that earning per month of the injured / petitioner is 14,468/- per month. 29. Further as per evidence on record, it is stated by the petitioner that due to such accident, he was unable to work and admitted to hospital from 19.09.2019 to 22.09.2019 and again from 09.10.2019 to 10.10.2019. It is further claimed that his treatment is continuing. As per record, treatment period of injured is ranging from 19.09.2019 to 20.10.2019. Further, as also argued by Ld. Counsel for petitioner MACT No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Page No. 9 of 25 that in case of present nature in which there is permanent disability also some guess work can also be employed having regard to the attending facts and circumstances. Accordingly, it is held that there is loss of income for 3 months in the present case. 30. Thus, it is held that total of the income of injured due to such accident is Rs. 43,404/- (Rs. 14,468/- x 3 months). Assessment of future loss of earnings due to permanent disability. 31. It was further observed by Hon'ble SC in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 32. Thus Loss of future Income: 15 % of [ (14,468/- X 12) X 15 ]= Rs. 3,90,636/-. CONTRIBUTORY NEGLIGENCE 39. 40. Before proceeding further, it may be noted that in Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri Vs. Karmasey Kungvargi Tak and Ors, it is held as under: "...9. The standard of reasonable man is as relevant in the case of plaintiff's contributory negligence as in the case of defendant's negligence. The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd.1 is worthy of quoting: "A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investi- gation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists MACT No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Page No. 14 of 25 and, if so , to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of con-tributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiffs share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. Contribu-tory negligence focuses on the conduct of the plaintiff. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." 41. Further, in Koosapa Poojari Vs. Sadabba & Ors., ILR 2003 KAR 1104, it is held as under: "Insofar as another duty cast on the pedestrian is concerned, it is needless to say that he has to give the driver a plenty of time to see him and slow down and start before Umesh Paswan vs . Shivam & Ors. on 12 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98978415/ 9 he attempts to cross or put one foot on the crossing. On the other hand, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for petitioner that in the case of Erudhaya Priya Vs. State Express Transport Corporation, Civil Appeal No. 2811-2812 of 2020, the Hon'ble three Judge Bench of Supreme Court held that interest @ 9% is fair. 48. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: Umesh Paswan vs . Shivam & Ors. on 12 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98978415/ 12 "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the MACT No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Page No. 20 of 25 Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of MACT No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Page No. 21 of 25 the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him. 52. The following conditions are to be adhered to by SBI, Saket Courts, Delhi with respect to the fixed deposits:- (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) Umesh Paswan vs . Shivam & Ors. on 12 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98978415/ 14 of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s). (b) The original fixed deposit shall be retained by the bank in safe custody. MACT No. 728/18 Umesh Paswan Vs. Shivam & Ors. Page No. 23 of 25 (g) The bank shall make an endorsement on the passbook of the claimant(s) to the effect that no cheque book and/or debit card have been issued and shall not be issued without the permission of the Court and claimant(s) shall produce the passbook with the necessary endorsement before the Court on the next date fixed for compliance.
